requirement:
A `list_files`, `ripgrep`, or `ast_grep` result MUST include `not_listed`, an
array of `{path, reason}` with reason `untracked`, naming each untracked file
inside the project that the listing would otherwise include or that contains a
match, so the model can tell that sources exist which it cannot read. It MUST
be omitted when there are none, and for a paged result it MUST appear on the
first page, continuing across subsequent pages when needed to obey the page
size limit. Page counts MUST include these entries as well as the ordinary
result entries, and each array MUST retain its order. It MUST NOT give those
files' contents, and they MUST NOT become
evidence inputs. Files excluded for another reason, such as a workspace disallow
rule or generated `evidence/` output, MUST NOT be read to find matches and MUST
NOT be listed.
rationale:
## Obligations and coverage

`requirements.authoring.not_listed` is satisfied by the marked implementation and tests.

| Obligation | Implementation and verification |
|---|---|
| Include `not_listed` for qualifying untracked files in `list_files` results. | `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[with_not_listed]` selects immediate listing children and constructs the array. `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[listings_and_searches_name_untracked_files_without_their_contents]` asserts the resulting paths. |
| Include it for untracked files containing a `ripgrep` match. | The same implementation's `NotListed::Text` branch reads candidate text and checks the pattern; the same test asserts both matching untracked paths. |
| Include it for untracked files containing an `ast_grep` match. | Its `NotListed::Rule` branch checks language coverage and structural matches; the same test asserts the Rust match and exercises all three tools with normalized requested paths. |
| Represent entries as `{path, reason}` with reason `untracked`. | `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[with_not_listed]` constructs exactly these fields. The tool test checks paths and every entry's reason. |
| Omit `not_listed` when there are no qualifying entries. | The helper returns the unchanged listing for an empty set; `src/authoring/pages.rs#impl[Listing]/fn[render]` also omits empty page arrays. The tool test checks no-match and empty-directory cases; the first-page test below checks omission on later pages. |
| Start `not_listed` on the first page. | `src/authoring/pages.rs#impl[Listing]/fn[with_not_listed]` prepends its entries. `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[not_listed_comes_on_the_first_page_within_the_page_limit]` verifies first-page placement and page sizes. |
| Continue it across pages when required by the size limit. | `src/authoring/pages.rs#impl[ResultPages]/fn[deliver]` uses `paginate` on the combined entries. `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[untracked_entries_page_without_tracked_entries_or_oversized_overhead]` exercises 1,000 untracked entries with zero, one, and 500 ordinary entries and checks every page's size and complete reconstruction. |
| Include untracked entries in total page counts. | `deliver` counts the combined vector; the 1,000-entry test asserts `total_entries`. |
| Include them in returned page counts. | `deliver` counts each combined page slice; that test asserts `returned_entries` equals the sum of both arrays' lengths. |
| Preserve ordinary-array order. | Prepending and consecutive pagination preserve relative order; the 1,000-entry test compares reconstructed ordinary entries with the original vector. |
| Preserve `not_listed` order. | The same operations preserve its order; that test also compares reconstructed untracked entries with the original vector. |
| Do not disclose untracked contents. | The tool helper emits only path/reason objects, not the text used for matching. The tool test asserts that the distinctive untracked contents do not appear in any of the three results. |
| Do not make these files evidence inputs. | Listing constructors use `evidence: false`, and `src/authoring/pages.rs#fn[delivered]` returns no inputs for these listings. Both the tool test and the 1,000-entry paging test assert empty evidence inputs. |
| Do not read files excluded for another reason to find matches. | The helper obtains candidates through `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[DiscoverySources]/fn[untracked]`, which filters through `considers` before the helper reads contents. `considers` applies discovery exclusions and workspace disallow rules. The tool test supplies matching disallowed and generated-evidence files and verifies the permitted results only. |
| Do not list those otherwise-excluded files. | The same candidate filtering excludes them before path construction; the tool test's exact expected arrays exclude both `secret.rs` and `evidence/note.txt`. |

The exclusion helpers are reachable from the marked `with_not_listed` implementation, and rendering, pagination, and evidence delivery are reachable from the marked paging implementations. `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[dispatch_paged]` confirms that all three tools invoke the helper and deliver its result through this paging machinery.

The paging notes and evidence-delivery behavior are covered by the co-marked `requirements.authoring.tool_descriptions.special_cases` and `requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`; they are not unexplained extra behavior. No acknowledged gaps were supplied or found.

text: :::{req} not_listed
A `list_files`, `ripgrep`, or `ast_grep` result MUST include `not_listed`, an
array of `{path, reason}` with reason `untracked`, naming each untracked file
inside the project that the listing would otherwise include or that contains a
match, so the model can tell that sources exist which it cannot read. It MUST
be omitted when there are none, and for a paged result it MUST appear on the
first page, continuing across subsequent pages when needed to obey the page
size limit. Page counts MUST include these entries as well as the ordinary
result entries, and each array MUST retain its order. It MUST NOT give those
files' contents, and they MUST NOT become
evidence inputs. Files excluded for another reason, such as a workspace disallow
rule or generated `evidence/` output, MUST NOT be read to find matches and MUST
NOT be listed.
:::{req} delivered_inputs
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs and additional reads, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.
:::{req} tool_descriptions.special_cases
Model tool descriptions SHOULD NOT explain cases the model meets only
occasionally, such as access policy, excluded or build-output paths, redaction,
paging, and failures, and the harness SHOULD explain each of these where it
occurs: in the tool error, or in a note in the result it affects. The model reads
every description on every assessment, so explaining rare cases there costs
attention on every review for a case most never meet, and access-policy wording
in particular can steer its reasoning away from the review. A tool whose purpose
is one of these cases, such as `next_page`, explains it in its description.
